item.title: Chaos and Bifurcations in Continuous Language-Model Feedback
item.description: Feeding a language model the probability-weighted average of its own token embeddings, as a smooth full-distribution variant of Soft Thinking does, turns inference into a smooth deterministic map. In thirteen of fifteen publicly released models from 0.5B to 72B parameters, from all three model families studied, temperature and steering move this loop between repeating text and chaos (temperature alone in eleven), organized as in low-dimensional maps: saddle-node bottlenecks, period-doubling cascades that approach Feigenbaum’s constant, and shrimp-shaped windows. Where the loop is chaotic, rounding differences as small as those from request batching can change what it writes; where it is periodic, they almost never do. In tests fixed in advance, reasoning models that solve 86 to 90% of grade-school math problems changed 14.5 and 19.5% of their answers when only the batch layout changed, and ordinary sampled reasoning changed a similar share, nearly all in long runs that reached the thinking or answer budget in at least one layout; the source depends on the model: in some, the changes are consistent with rounding carried through long feedback, while in QwQ-32B and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B the thinking loop itself slowly amplifies tiny differences, and a relative displacement far below rounding alone changes about 14 and 18% of their answers, respectively. The loop is not ordinary sampled generation.
